messages:
Nora Kim: Heads-up: product asked for a per-request compatibility score (v1->v2) so they can show "upgrade risk" for tenants. Runtime can compute a tiny heuristic but emitting every decision will blow up telemetry storage and ES ingestion costs. Thoughts?

Jacob Lee: Agree it's useful, but we should sample. My proposal: emit full decision events for 1% of requests + all errors. For the rest emit only aggregated counters per minute (tenant, model, bucket). That keeps request-level traces for debugging without full ingestion.

Priya Nair: Product wants deterministic heatmap in console (by route, by tenant, last 7 days). Aggregates are fine. UI needs counts for "compatible", "minor-diff", "incompatible" per model. We can derive those from sampled traces plus aggregated counters.

Nora Kim: Concern: some tenants are low-volume so 1% sampling yields nothing. Suggest hybrid: if tenant_qps < threshold, sample at 100% for that tenant for a short window when they enable "migration preview". Otherwise 1%.

Marco Alvarez: Storage/cost side: we should store full traces in cheap long-term blob (S3) and keep only indexed summary in ES. Decision event body can be zipped json and stored keyed by decision_id. Console modal can fetch on demand. This reduces ES docs but keeps fidelity.

SREbot: Note: PLAT-5301 created: decision-event-sampling + s3-archive + aggregated-rollup.

Jacob Lee: Also need privacy check: some decision traces include prompt snippets for debugging. We must strip prompt text before archiving; only keep hashes/lengths and token counts. Add opt-in to keep sanitized prompt for customer support.

Priya Nair: UX detail: console heatmap should default to aggregation and show a "show sampled traces" button which fetches decision_ids (needs signed debug token). We'll add a toggle "increase sampling for this tenant (48h)".

Nora Kim: Operational: add a new telemetry gauge `compatibility_score_coverage_pct` and alert if sampling falls below target per-tenant cohort. Also track cost delta monthly.

Marco Alvarez: Implementation sketch: 1) Router computes compatibility_score (0..1) and assigns bucket label. 2) Router emits lightweight counter to kafka: (tenant, model, bucket). 3) Router writes full trace to s3 with decision_id if sampled. 4) Rollup job writes to metrics store every minute. 5) Console queries metrics store and fetches s3 objects on demand.

Jacob Lee: Backwards compatibility: don't add new required headers. Use internal fields only. For debug APIs require admin token. Also add `X-Compat-Sampled: 1` header when we sampled the request so clients know.

Priya Nair: Product asks for rollout plan: start with 5% sampling + s3 arch for 2 weeks in staging, then ramp to 1% prod with low-volume tenant hybrid. I'll draft copy and mock.

Nora Kim: Ok owners: Jacob (sampling + router change), Marco (s3 arch + cost calc), Priya (console mock + product copy). Let's reconvene after staging run.
